headline: Microsoft counted more than 1 million chief executive impersonation scam emails in three days while Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei put an AI agent swarm capable of taking over the internet six to 12 months away.

emerging_trends.text: Microsoft's count of more than 1 million chief executive impersonation emails and the passkey enrollment lures aimed at the same tenants show attackers spending their effort on the person sitting in front of the login screen.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Passkey Lures and CEO Impersonation Hit Microsoft 365

emerging_trends.text: Dario Amodei asks the industry for six to 12 months of safety work while his own company keeps publishing accounts of Claude helping intruders and weapons builders, a gap between capability and control that lands on every enterprise running the models.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Amodei Warns of Agent Swarms Within a Year

emerging_trends.text: The China-aligned crew behind GrayRabbit picked Sogou Input Method, software that sits on millions of Windows desktops, which puts espionage access one client-side bug away for any organization whose staff types Chinese.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Sogou Input Method Flaw Delivers GrayRabbit

topics.title: Passkey Lures and CEO Impersonation Hit Microsoft 365
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft put numbers on the fraud wave on September 13, 2026, counting more than 1 million scam emails sent between August 3 and August 5, 2026 by operators who posed as chief executives and pushed the messages through third-party email delivery services, a campaign running alongside the passkey and single sign-on social engineering that ShinyHunters, Helix, and other extortion crews aim at corporate Microsoft accounts.
topics.summary: The passkey lures talk employees into enrolling an authentication method the attacker controls, which yields durable access to Microsoft 365, SharePoint, OneDrive, and mail; the invoice and payment scams stack legitimacy tricks with AI help. Administrators should review recent authentication method enrollments and restrict which outside senders may deliver mail under the company's domain.

sources.title: Attackers Use Passkey Phishing to Hijack Microsoft Cloud Accounts and Exfiltrate Data
Passkey-themed phishing attacks lead to Microsoft 365 data theft
Microsoft sees some new wrinkles in invoice-scam emails

topics.title: Frontier Models Learn to Work on Humans
topics.latest_developments: Fred Heiding of Menlo Park Intelligence told the Dark Reading News Desk that his tests of frontier models measure their ability to steer human behavior and cultivate emotional dependency in a target, and Bruce Schneier posted the DEF CON talk he gave last month on what follows when AI systems become the hackers, which passed 100,000 YouTube views within days.
topics.summary: Persuasion now counts as an attack capability of large language models, on top of the exploit code they write for intruders. Dark Reading separately warned that adversaries can bend the reasoning of AI defensive tools to move through a network quietly, which puts every model an enterprise runs under the governance question.

sources.title: Why AI Is So Good at Scamming Humans
My Talk at DEF CON
AI Governance Can't Wait

topics.title: Meta Faces AI Image Suit and Abuse Video Failures
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported that Meta has failed to stop AI-generated videos of child abuse from spreading across its platforms, days after plaintiffs filed a proposed class action accusing the company of harvesting Facebook and Instagram photos to train its AI image-generation models and to build NameTag, an unreleased face recognition feature.
topics.summary: Meta's generative image work now draws pressure from two sides: civil claims over the photographs that trained the models and moderation failures on the synthetic media those tools help produce. Both threads feed the coming rules on training data and synthetic content.

sources.title: From Hacks to Bioweapons, Claude Misuse Is Now Everywhere
Meta Sued Over Training Data for Its AI and Face-Recognition Systems

topics.title: Amodei Warns of Agent Swarms Within a Year
topics.latest_developments: Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, said on September 13, 2026 that within six to 12 months an AI system could direct a swarm of agents able to take over the entire internet, and he asked the industry to give safety measures time to catch up.
topics.summary: Amodei runs the company that has spent the past week documenting its own model rebuilding malware for Russian operators, extracting secrets from 1.8 million Android applications, and helping users in Houthi-held Yemen test a guided rocket. His timeline puts a date on the distance between what the models do and what their builders can control.

sources.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei Says AI Industry Needs to Give Safety Measures Time to Catch Up

topics.title: Sogou Input Method Flaw Delivers GrayRabbit
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer identified the bug behind the China-aligned espionage campaign on September 13, 2026 as CVE-2026-51990, a critical flaw in Tencent's Sogou Input Method for Windows that operators exploit to plant the GrayRabbit backdoor.
topics.summary: Sogou Input Method ranks among the most widely used ways to type Chinese characters on Windows, and the group UNC3569 starts each intrusion with a crafted link and finishes with a backdoor that carries the logged-in user's full rights. Organizations with Chinese-language staff should update the software or pull it off their desktops.

sources.title: Hackers exploit Tencent app flaw to deploy GrayRabbit malware

topics.title: NSA Splits Into Five Mission Centers
topics.latest_developments: The Record reported on September 13, 2026 that the National Security Agency is moving quickly through a thorough reorganization that will build five mission centers, among them one for cyber and one for artificial intelligence.
topics.summary: The NSA runs signals intelligence collection and, through its Cybersecurity Collaboration Center, the defensive work that reaches United States companies and defense contractors. A restructuring at that scale moves the people and reporting lines industry calls for nation-state threat intelligence.

sources.title: Thorough reorganization at NSA will create five 'mission centers,' including cyber and AI

topics.title: Iran Bounty, QTFY Ties, and InjectEave
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported that the United States has posted a $10 million bounty for information on an Iranian cyber official whom it declines to name publicly, that researchers documented the military ties of the Chinese hacking group QTFY, and that a technique called InjectEave joins phishing which hides invisible Unicode characters to clear mail filters.
topics.summary: The items trace state hacking crews back to their governments and show filter evasion moving down into character encoding, where a gateway that never normalizes text scores a malicious message as clean. Mail security teams should confirm their filters normalize Unicode before they score a message.

sources.title: In Other News: InjectEave Attack, SIM Swapper Sentenced, Glasswing Findings Review

topics.title: Mullenweg Says He Runs Automattic Again
topics.latest_developments: Matt Mullenweg says he is back in control of Automattic, three days after the company's board voted to put him on leave, and workers there told 404 Media the company has absorbed years of chaotic leadership decisions.
topics.summary: Automattic owns WordPress.com and employs the people who operate WordPress.org, the channel that pushes plugin updates to millions of sites and that began screening every plugin release automatically last week. Who holds authority over that pipeline is a supply chain question for every organization running WordPress.

sources.title: Automattic's Matt Mullenweg Claims He's Back 'In Control'

business_politics.title: Gulf Talks on Hormuz Collapse Into Delay
business_politics.latest_developments: Gulf states postponed the crunch meeting with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz impasse for lack of consensus, the Financial Times reported Sunday, September 13, setting back efforts to restore shipping through the waterway.
business_politics.summary: Iran's contested management of the Strait of Hormuz has kept roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil hostage, and the International Energy Agency has already written off a reopening this year. The Economist reported the same day that the Houthis' rapid advance in Yemen, an embarrassment for Saudi Arabia, hands Tehran further leverage over the region's shipping lanes.

sources.title: Gulf states postpone talks with Iran over Hormuz impasse
The Houthis’ shock advance in Yemen gives Iran new leverage

business_politics.title: Trump Presses Kyiv to Stop Hitting Russian Refineries
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump called on Ukraine Sunday, September 13, to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries, blaming those attacks for record diesel prices, hours after a Russian drone hit a train line near the Polish border that David Petraeus, Boris Johnson, and Carl Bildt had traveled moments earlier.
business_politics.summary: Ukrainian long-range strikes have knocked out Russian refining capacity through the summer, tightening a global diesel market already squeezed by the Gulf war, and U.S. retail diesel set a record above $6 a gallon on September 11. Trump's demand puts the White House at odds with Kyiv while Russia escalates attacks on civilian and rail targets.

sources.title: Trump calls on Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries
Dueling Airstrikes Fuel Angst as Russia-Ukraine War Escalates
Russia strikes Ukraine train line moments after foreign dignitaries pass

business_politics.title: Brics Closes Ranks Over the Gulf War
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Sunday, September 13, that the Brics summit produced rare unanimity, with the bloc pressing for peace in the Gulf and lining up against American tariffs and sanctions.
business_politics.summary: Brics, the bloc built around Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, normally splits over agendas, and worry about the widening Iran conflict, U.S. tariffs, and U.S. sanctions handed this summit an easy consensus. Rivalry between India and China over trade and regional influence still caps how far their rapprochement runs.

sources.title: ‘Trumpism’ spawns rare unity at Brics summit
Brics push for Gulf peace as war worries mount

business_politics.title: A Banking Scandal Reaches Brazil's Supreme Court
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Sunday, September 13, that a banking scandal has pulled Brazil's Supreme Federal Court into an unprecedented crisis, with a bitter feud between justices spilling into public view.
business_politics.summary: Brazil's Supreme Federal Court settles the country's biggest political and financial disputes, and the fight among its justices lands weeks before the October presidential election, which the crisis could sway. Investors hold heavy exposure to Brazilian sovereign debt and to the banks now caught up in the affair.

sources.title: Brazil banking scandal engulfs Supreme Court

business.title: Trade Schools Fill Up as AI Unsettles Office Work
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Sunday, September 13, that trade and technical schools are posting enrollment increases as students weigh artificial intelligence against the security of white-collar careers.
business.summary: Students choosing welding, electrical, and other skilled trades over four-year degrees cite the reach of artificial intelligence into entry-level office jobs, along with the cost of college. The shift reaches Western Pennsylvania employers who have spent years short of licensed tradespeople.

sources.title: Trade schools see enrollment bumps as students worry about AI, job security in white-collar work

business.title: Superloads Come With the Data Centers
business.latest_developments: TribLive's editorial board wrote Sunday, September 13, that the oversized hauls now crossing Western Pennsylvania roads are an inseparable part of the data center buildout, citing the Pew Research Center's count of roughly 1,500 data centers in development nationwide.
business.summary: Transporters started moving superloads carrying equipment as heavy as 380 tons through the region this month, slowing traffic on several busy roads across multiple counties for months. The deliveries feed the computing campuses developers are building around Pittsburgh, and the editorial argues residents weighing those projects should count the road disruption as part of the price.

sources.title: Editorial: Big loads are big part of data centers

around_town.title: NASA Flies Over the Steelers' Home Opener
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Sunday, September 13, that NASA conducted its first flyover of an NFL game as tailgaters packed the North Shore lots for the Steelers' 1 p.m. home opener at Acrisure Stadium.
around_town.summary: The opener against the Atlanta Falcons drew the season's first full crowd to the North Shore, filling the parking lots, bars, and restaurants around Acrisure Stadium hours before kickoff. The flyover marked the space agency's debut over a professional football stadium.

sources.title: Steelers’ home opener brings crowds — and NASA’s first NFL flyover

around_town.title: Measles Kills a Jefferson County Woman
around_town.latest_developments: The Jefferson County coroner confirmed Sunday, September 13, that a 40-year-old woman died Saturday from complications of measles, the county's first measles death.
around_town.summary: Pennsylvania has counted 676 measles cases this year, the most of any state, and about 100 of those arrived in the week before September 11. Two infants died of measles-related causes in the state last month, and this death is the first adult the outbreak has claimed.

sources.title: Jefferson County Coroner reports county's first measles-related death
Jefferson County officials confirm first measles-related death

around_town.title: Another Line of Storms Sunday Night
around_town.latest_developments: The National Weather Service posted a severe thunderstorm warning for parts of Allegheny, Butler, and Beaver counties until 7 p.m. Sunday, September 13, as a line of storms carrying damaging wind, hail, and heavy rain crossed the region ahead of a cold front, and WTAE expects a brief fall cool down behind it.
around_town.summary: Fast-moving water flooded roads and damaged homes, vehicles, and businesses across Washington and Allegheny counties Saturday night, and the flood-control work the city of Washington has planned keeps slipping as the rain returns; the city declared a state of emergency. Feels-like readings reached the mid-80s during the Steelers' 1 p.m. kickoff before the front arrived.

sources.title: Sunday starts dry, but another line of showers will move through during evening hours
‘Just despicable’: Washington residents struggle with continued floods caused by summer downpours
Pittsburgh: Muggy with sun and clouds for Steelers Sunday
Western Pennsylvania gets brief fall cool down after Sunday storms

around_town.title: Clover Commons Residents Press for House Bill 1250
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Sunday, September 13, that nearly 60 residents of Clover Commons in Plum took to the streets of their community last week over rising land rent and asked Pennsylvania senators to pass House Bill 1250.
around_town.summary: The Clover Commons residents own their homes and rent the ground beneath them, and the seniors among them live on fixed incomes that the rent increases outrun. House Bill 1250 would hold that land rent in check, and the protesters want the state Senate to move it.

sources.title: Senior residents on fixed incomes urge state senators to pass House Bill 1250, ensuring rent doesn’t have to go up

events.title: 'America's Tapestry' Opens at Seton Hill
events.latest_developments: The traveling exhibition "America's Tapestry" opened Sunday, September 13, at Seton Hill University in Greensburg, and TribLive covered the opening.
events.summary: "America's Tapestry" gathers textile panels depicting ordinary people who shaped the American Revolution, one panel per state. Textile artist Rachel Weinblum, who stitched part of the Pennsylvania panel, attended the Greensburg opening and saw her work on display for the first time.

sources.title: ‘America’s Tapestry’ depicts ordinary heroes of American Revolution

events.title: Game Lands Driving Tours Open September 20
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Sunday, September 13, that the Pennsylvania Game Commission will again open state game lands to self-guided driving tours starting Sunday, September 20.
events.summary: The Game Commission lets drivers roll through wildlife habitat on state game lands roads normally closed to vehicles, a fall tradition aimed at people who want to watch wildlife without hiking. The tours begin Sunday, September 20, and run through the fall.

sources.title: Game commission offers self-guided game lands tours this fall

around_teams.title: Watt and Highsmith Carry the McCarthy Debut
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette graded T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith at A-plus in its Sunday, September 13, report card on the Steelers' opener against the Atlanta Falcons, crediting Watt's pick-six for deciding the game, while columnist Noah Hiles wrote that Mike McCarthy's first game felt unfortunately familiar.
around_teams.summary: Watt, 31, returned an interception for a touchdown and added two sacks and two tackles for loss in his first game under McCarthy, with Aaron Rodgers at quarterback at Acrisure Stadium. Hiles argued the sloppy offense and reliance on the pass rush echoed the pattern of recent Steelers seasons, leaving McCarthy's promised new standard unproven.

sources.title: Steelers report card: T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith deliver A-plus performances against the Falcons
Noah Hiles: A win is a win, but the first game of the McCarthy era felt unfortunately familiar
T.J. Watt’s dominant day helps the Steelers begin the Mike McCarthy era with a win

around_teams.title: Porter Sits Out While Healthy Enough to Play
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers ruled out cornerback Joey Porter Jr. for the opener Sunday, September 13, and sources told the Post-Gazette he is healthy enough to play, tying the absence to his unresolved contract.
around_teams.summary: Porter, the 2023 second-round pick and a starting cornerback, said Friday, September 11, that he felt "not really" optimistic about signing a new deal before the season began. The standoff leaves Pittsburgh's secondary short of its top outside corner in the first week.

sources.title: Joey Porter Jr. was ruled out for the Steelers’ opener, but sources say he is healthy enough to play
Joey Porter Jr. is 'not really' optimistic he will sign a new contract before the Steelers' opener

around_teams.title: Kelly's Bench Move Salvages the Cubs Series
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Sunday, September 13, that manager Don Kelly sent Brandon Lowe up as a pinch hitter and leaned on his bullpen to keep the Chicago Cubs from sweeping the Pirates at Wrigley Field, a day after second-guessing his own bullpen call.
around_teams.summary: Bubba Chandler started the finale for Pittsburgh, which closed a six-game road trip through Chicago against the White Sox and Cubs. Kelly's relief decision in Saturday's blown save drew his own criticism before Sunday's moves worked.

sources.title: Brandon Lowe and the bullpen help the Pirates avoid a sweep against the Cubs

team_usa.title: U.S. Women Win a Fifth Straight World Cup
team_usa.latest_developments: The United States beat France 97-79 on Sunday, September 13, in Germany to claim its fifth consecutive FIBA Women's World Cup title, with Breanna Stewart scoring 22 points and Jackie Young adding 18.
team_usa.summary: Kara Lawson's team ran the tournament unbeaten, surviving Italy 55-52, routing Hungary 108-56 in the quarterfinals, and holding off Spain 76-66 in the semifinals. The final was a rematch of the 2024 Olympic gold medal game, and Spain took bronze by beating host Germany 81-58 earlier Sunday.

sources.title: Team USA proves 'the standard' again with 5th straight World Cup gold
Spain beats Germany to win bronze at women's FIBA World Cup

team_usa.title: Jefferson-Wooden Completes the Sprint Double
team_usa.latest_developments: Melissa Jefferson-Wooden ran 21.47 seconds in the 200 meters Sunday, September 13, at the Ultimate Championship, the fourth-fastest time in history, finishing a $300,000 weekend.
team_usa.summary: Jefferson-Wooden had won the 100 meters Saturday, September 12, in a world-leading 10.62 seconds at the same meet, where Kenny Bednarek also took a title. The double gives the American sprinter the season's fastest marks at both distances.

sources.title: Jefferson-Wooden clocks 21.47 in 200-meter run at Ultimate Championship
Jefferson-Wooden, Bednarek capture Ultimate Championship wins

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: The Hater's Guide To Broadcom
reading.summary: Zitron dissects Broadcom under chief executive Hock Tan, opening with Tan's 2024 coffee chat introducing his management style to employees of the freshly acquired VMware and its 100-acre Palo Alto campus. He argues the company's model runs on buying entrenched software businesses and squeezing them.

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: The iPhone Duo, The Intelligent Personal Hub, Apple Watch Audio Intelligence
reading.summary: Ben Thompson credits Apple's latest launch as another demonstration of hardware and software integration done well, from the iPhone Duo to Apple Watch audio intelligence. He argues Apple's largest artificial-intelligence blind spot is its conviction that apps remain the organizing layer of computing.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport responds to Anthropic employees who said publicly that the systems they build could kill billions, calling superintelligence a story the industry tells itself. He argues the pursuit still does real damage through the resources, expectations, and political capital it consumes.
